headline: US futures edge higher ahead of the June jobs report (8:30am ET), with chips still under pressure after Wednesday's sector selloff but broader rotation into non-tech names keeping the S&P near its prior-session close.
stance: The session pivot is 8:30am ET: June nonfarm payrolls, released a day early for the Independence Day holiday. Consensus sits around 100K–115K (down from May's 172K) with unemployment steady at 4.3%; a beat risks accelerating Fed rate-hike pricing, while a miss opens a soft-landing window and could lift bonds and gold. Pre-market futures (as of ~6:45am ET) are modestly positive — S&P +0.14%, Nasdaq-100 +0.23%, Dow +0.1% — as markets look past Wednesday's chip rout and await the data for the week's directional cue.

news.head: Chip selloff ripples into Asia
news.body: Wednesday's semiconductor rout — Micron -10.6%, AMD -6.9%, Intel -9%, the semiconductor ETF SMH -5.4% — spread overnight to South Korea, where Samsung fell more than 7% and SK Hynix sank over 9%, triggering a brief trading halt on the Kospi.

news.head: Meta jumps, non-tech holds
news.body: Meta Platforms surged nearly 9% after announcing plans to launch a cloud business and sell excess AI computing capacity, with Microsoft +3% and Apple +2% helping cushion the broader market decline; the Dow touched an intraday record of 52,742 before retreating.

news.head: NFP due 8:30am ET
news.body: The June jobs report is published a day early ahead of Friday's Independence Day closure; consensus is ~100K–115K new jobs and a 4.3% unemployment rate — well below May's 172K, but still above the trailing 12-month average.

news.head: ADP miss stokes hopes for softer Fed
news.body: Wednesday's ADP private payrolls showed only 98K jobs added in June, below estimates, giving markets a hint that Friday's official print could disappoint and potentially ease rate-hike pressure on the Fed.

news.head: Fed Chair Warsh at ECB forum
news.body: Fed Chair Kevin Warsh told the ECB's Sintra symposium that inflation expectations have eased over the past month, but he reaffirmed commitment to price stability and declined to provide forward guidance on rates — the market still prices more than a 60% chance of at least one hike in 2026.

news.head: US-Iran talks progress, oil slides
news.body: Indirect US-Iran negotiations in Qatar showed progress on shipping passage through the Strait of Hormuz, pulling Brent crude down toward $71; WTI closed at $68.09 (prior cash close) as geopolitical risk premium continues to drain from energy markets.

news.head: Bending Spoons IPO pops 42%
news.body: Italian software company Bending Spoons — owner of AOL and Vimeo — debuted on the Nasdaq and surged 42% on its first day of US trading, opening at $31 against a $29 IPO price.

news.head: SpaceX set to join Nasdaq-100 on July 7
news.body: Index-tracking funds are expected to begin purchasing SpaceX shares after the close on July 6, with the stock officially entering the Nasdaq-100 before trading on July 7.

implications: A jobs print above ~130K would likely push the 10Y yield (prior close: 4.48%) higher and squeeze gold, which rebounded above $4,000 in overnight trade after briefly dipping below it Wednesday.
A print at or below 85K could reprice the Fed path dovishly — supportive for rate-sensitive small-caps and bonds, and a tailwind for gold and the Euro.
Chip names are already a one-day loser; a soft jobs number could trigger a rotation back into semis on 'peak-hawkish' logic, while a hot number would likely deepen the tech drawdown.

USD/JPY (prior close: 162.55) sits at a 99th-percentile three-year extreme for yen weakness — verbal intervention risk from Tokyo is elevated; any dollar softness post-NFP could see sharp yen snapback.

Positioning: Speculators have almost no bullish bets left in Nasdaq-100 futures (4th percentile, 3-year range) and Russell 2000 futures (2nd percentile) — a contrarian floor suggesting professional shorts are extended and squeeze risk is present if the jobs print is benign. Copper speculator positioning is at the 95th percentile — speculators are heavily positioned long copper, a contrarian warning. British pound specs are at their most extended short in three years (1st percentile) — a contrarian-bullish lean for GBP.

watch.head: 8:30am ET — June NFP
watch.body: The single biggest market-mover of the week: consensus ~100K–115K jobs, unemployment 4.3%; a wide miss or beat will reprice equities, bonds, the dollar, and gold simultaneously.

watch.head: 10Y yield (4.48% prior close)
watch.body: Watch whether yields hold below the psychologically important 4.50% level post-NFP; a break higher would increase pressure on high-multiple tech and growth stocks.

watch.head: USD/JPY (162.55 prior close)
watch.body: At a 40-year yen weakness extreme; any dovish NFP surprise could accelerate yen strength, unwinding carry trades and creating cross-asset volatility.

watch.head: Gold (~$4,000–$4,045 overnight)
watch.body: Gold rebounded toward $4,045 overnight after briefly breaking below $4,000 Wednesday; the NFP print is the binary — strong jobs data risks re-testing $4,000 support, weak data could reignite the bull trend.

watch.head: Chip sector (SMH) open
watch.body: After a 5.4% one-day loss Wednesday and further Asian selling overnight, watch whether US semi names stabilize or extend losses at the open — the sector's direction will shape Nasdaq-100 performance for the day.

watch.head: US markets close Friday Jul 4
watch.body: Today is the last full trading session of the week; any position-squaring ahead of the long weekend could amplify post-NFP moves in both directions.

sections.title: Macro & Rates
bullets: 10Y Treasury yield holds at 4.48% (prior cash close), near a 10bps rebound from Monday's seven-week low of 4.36%, as hawkish Fed repricing and a resilient labor market keep upward pressure on longer-dated bonds.
2Y yield at 4.17% (prior cash close) gives a 31bp 10Y-2Y spread — technically positive (not inverted), but historically thin, reflecting the market's uncertainty about the growth vs. inflation mix.
Fed Chair Warsh said inflation risks are easing but offered no rate-cut pivot; the Fed held at 3.50%–3.75% in June and markets still price more than a 60% probability of at least one hike in 2026.

10Y breakeven inflation at 2.23% (prior close) — the bond market's inflation expectation is only modestly above the Fed's 2% target, signaling the market does not believe energy-driven CPI will persist.
Real rates at 2.25% (prior close) remain restrictive and act as a headwind for gold and long-duration equity valuations (CAPE at 41.7x is elevated).
The term premium — the extra yield investors demand for holding long bonds — sits at 68.4 basis points, reflecting lingering fiscal and inflation uncertainty.
MOVE index (bond-market volatility gauge) at 68.6 (prior close) is subdued, suggesting the options market is not pricing a catastrophic rates move from today's NFP.
sections.positioning: Speculators in 3-month SOFR interest-rate futures are at the 1st percentile of their 3-year net-position range — speculators have almost no bullish bets left, a contrarian floor suggesting rate-cut risk is already priced aggressively short.

sections.title: Equity Markets
bullets: S&P 500 prior cash close: 7,483.23; Nasdaq-100 prior cash close: 26,040.03; Dow prior cash close: 52,305.24 — all three indices ended Wednesday lower (S&P -0.22%, Nasdaq -0.66%, Dow -0.03%) after the Dow hit a record intraday high of 52,742.
Pre-market futures (as of ~6:45am ET): S&P +0.14%, Nasdaq-100 +0.23%, Dow +0.11% — fractionally positive as markets await the jobs report.
H1 2026 scorecard: S&P +9.6%, Nasdaq +12.8%, Dow +8.9%, Russell 2000 +22% — the best small-cap first half since 1991.
62% of S&P 500 stocks trade above their 50-day moving average and 63.1% above their 200-day average (prior close) — healthy breadth even as the mega-cap chip trade corrects.
VIX at 16.59 (prior close) is well below stress levels, suggesting investors see Wednesday's chip selloff as healthy profit-taking rather than a systemic unwind.

SKEW index at 154.8 (prior close) — a high reading that reflects institutional demand for downside protection (tail-risk hedging), even as the VIX stays low; the two together signal calm surface, hidden caution underneath.
The chip rout hit Micron (-10.6%), AMD (-6.9%), Intel (-9%), and Sandisk (-10.6%) Wednesday; Meta's +9% on cloud expansion news and Microsoft +3% partially offset the index-level damage.
Equity-credit correlation at 0.709 (prior close) — stocks and credit spreads are moving together, which means a deterioration in credit would quickly transmit into equities.
sections.positioning: Speculators in Nasdaq-100 futures are at the 4th percentile of their 3-year positioning range — speculators have almost no bullish bets left, a contrarian floor. Shorts are not heavy in absolute terms (days-to-cover light across most setups) but any upside catalyst could force rapid short-covering. VIX futures positioning is also extended short (12th percentile), meaning a vol spike would catch most specs offside.

single_name.note: Taiwan Semiconductor (TSM) — the world's dominant chip foundry, trading above its 200-day line despite the sector rout; large off-exchange block buying (quiet institutional accumulation) and a burst of unusual options activity were both live as of Jul 1 scan. Short interest is low (1.8 days to cover) so shorts are light with minimal squeeze risk — institutions appear to be building a position into the sector pullback. Score: 8/10, signal fresh.

sections.title: Credit & Liquidity
bullets: HY-IG spread at 275 bps (as of Jun 30) — the gap between junk-bond yields and investment-grade yields is the market's live stress gauge; a reading here is moderate and not signaling imminent credit distress.
IG option-adjusted spread at 76 bps (Jun 30) — investment-grade credit is priced close to tight historical levels, consistent with a low-default environment.
FRA-OIS and SOFR-OIS funding spreads both at just 5 bps (Jun 30) — bank-to-bank lending stress is essentially zero; interbank plumbing is clear.
Commercial paper funding spread at 18 bps (Jun 26) — short-term corporate borrowing costs are benign.

Overnight Reverse Repo (RRP) facility usage: just $1 billion (Jul 1) — near zero, meaning money-market funds have fully deployed cash into the market rather than parking it at the Fed; a positive liquidity signal for risk assets.
Bank reserves at $2,951 billion (Jun 24) — ample system liquidity; the Fed's balance sheet is still large enough to cushion any funding shocks.

Treasury General Account (TGA) at $919 billion (Jun 24) — a large TGA balance means the Treasury has firepower; as it draws down to pay bills, it injects cash into the banking system (a liquidity tailwind).
Financial conditions indexes (ANFCI -0.49, STLFSI -0.64, both Jun 26) remain well in accommodative territory — looser than neutral despite the Fed holding rates steady.

single_name.note: Scorpio Tankers (STNG) — product-tanker operator exposed to Strait of Hormuz shipping flows; large off-exchange block buying and unusual options activity live as of Jul 1 scan, with two insider buying signals fired. Trades above its 200-day line. Short interest manageable at 4.0 days to cover. Progress in US-Iran talks is a direct read-through to tanker rate normalization. Score: 5/10, signal fresh.
